changelog: **The scheduler takes the `'scheduler'` lease on every tick (#1676):** every schedule in the product (22) is declared once in `src/lib/jobs/schedules.ts` with its cadence and its reason. Three are now **queue** schedules — the dead-letter alert, the audit stream tick and the new nightly `JobRun` prune: a 30 s tick (`src/lib/jobs/scheduler.ts`, started from `/api/cron/start`) on the lease holder enqueues each due slot under `idempotencyKey = <key>:<slotISO>`, remembers it in the new `ScheduleState` table (one conditional write, never backwards) and catches up a missed slot (`catchUp: 'latest'` enqueues only the most recent one; `'none'` skips). The first sight of a schedule baselines instead of firing on deploy. The other 19 still run on node-cron, but through `scheduleLeased()` (`src/lib/jobs/leasedCron.ts`), so their bodies run on the lease holder only. Slot maths is dependency-free (`src/lib/jobs/cronSlot.ts`, process local time = UTC in the containers, identical to node-cron). With that in, `infra/deploy-prod.sh` no longer starts replica ≥2 with `CRON_ENABLED=0`; a graceful SIGTERM releases the lease so the other replica takes over at once, a dead one loses it within 90 s. `CRON_ENABLED=0` / no `CRON_SECRET` still start nothing.
